title: Air Traffic Control Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
3. MOS 5950, Air Traffic Control Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC
AVN

    a. Summary. Air Traffic Control (ATC) Systems Officers supervise and
coordinate the installation, sighting, operation, training, maintenance, and
repair of ATC and meteorology and oceanography (METOC) systems and equipment.
Must possess a detailed, working knowledge of all Navy sponsored aviation
maintenance programs and processes governed by the Naval Aviation Maintenance
Program Manual and familiarization with the ground equipment maintenance
program. Fleet marine forces billet assignments for this officer will be in
the marine air control group. Non-Fleet Marine Forces billet assignments for
this officer include maintenance billets at marine corps air stations, marine
corps air facilities, and marine corps installation command. The ATC Systems
Officer should complete the Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Management
Course and Joint Aviation Supply and Maintenance Material Management Course
after selection to warrant officer. PMOS is not dependent upon the
completion of these courses. Upon appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5950
is assigned.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (3) This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who previously
were qualified in the enlisted MOSs 5951, 5952, 5953, or 5954.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Mangers
Course (N23KCN2).



                                         1-234                        Enclosure (1)
 1134                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

            (3) MOS is assigned after Marine is promoted to warrant officer.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Supervises operation and maintenance of specific ATC and METOC
systems and common ground equipment used in Marine ATC companies or in Marine
ATC facilities.

        (2) Manages the status of equipment, progress of work, repair parts
requirements, training and qualification of maintenance personnel, and
advises on all technical matters pertaining to the ATC and METOC systems and
equipment.

        (3) Provides information concerning capabilities, limitations, and
reliability of ATC and METOC systems and equipment.

        (4) Communications planner for ATC services in expeditionary
amphibious base operations and ensures command and control for littoral
operations in a contested environment.

        (5) Collects and disseminates technical instructions and directives
applicable to the maintenance and operation of systems and equipment.

        (6) Prepares timely estimates and justification for funds required
for the maintenance of installed systems and equipment.

        (7) Maintains authorized allowances of tools and test and support
equipment.

            (8) Administers the preventive and corrective maintenance program.

            (9) Conducts maintenance management of assigned equipment.

            (10) Collects and analyzes maintenance data for reports.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Mangers, All Others 11-9199.

        (2) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 49-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Aviation Meteorological Equipment Technician, 5951.

            (2) Air Traffic Control Navigational Aids Technician, 5952.

            (3) Air Traffic Control Radar Technician, 5953.

            (4) Air Traffic Control Communications Technician, 5954.




                                        1-235                          Enclosure (1)
 1134                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L

matches: Coordinate communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel.

Air Traffic Control (ATC) Systems Officers supervise and coordinate the installation, sighting, operation, training, maintenance, and repair of ATC and meteorology and oceanography (METOC) systems and equipment.
Inspect completed work to certify that maintenance meets standards and that aircraft are ready for operation.

Must possess a detailed, working knowledge of all Navy sponsored aviation maintenance programs and processes governed by the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program Manual and familiarization with the ground equipment maintenance program.
Provide on-the-job training to new air traffic controllers.

The ATC Systems Officer should complete the Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Management Course and Joint Aviation Supply and Maintenance Material Management Course after selection to warrant officer.
Design and oversee testing, installation, and repair of marine apparatus and equipment.
d. Duties (1) Supervises operation and maintenance of specific ATC and METOC systems and common ground equipment used in Marine ATC companies or in Marine ATC facilities.
Oversee the maintenance and repair of machinery, equipment, and electrical and mechanical systems.

(2) Manages the status of equipment, progress of work, repair parts requirements, training and qualification of maintenance personnel, and advises on all technical matters pertaining to the ATC and METOC systems and equipment.
Evaluate sources of information to determine any limitations, in terms of reliability or usability.
(3) Provides information concerning capabilities, limitations, and reliability of ATC and METOC systems and equipment.
Oversee all communications within specifically assigned territories.
(4) Communications planner for ATC services in expeditionary amphibious base operations and ensures command and control for littoral operations in a contested environment.
Authorize maintenance activities on units or changes in equipment or system operational status.
(5) Collects and disseminates technical instructions and directives applicable to the maintenance and operation of systems and equipment.
Estimate, order, pick up, deliver, and install materials and supplies needed to maintain equipment in good working condition.
(6) Prepares timely estimates and justification for funds required for the maintenance of installed systems and equipment.
Clean or maintain tools or test equipment.
(7) Maintains authorized allowances of tools and test and support equipment.
Perform preventive or corrective maintenance on robotic systems or components.
(8) Administers the preventive and corrective maintenance program.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
(9) Conducts maintenance management of assigned equipment.
Maintain accurate, detailed reports and records.
(10) Collects and analyzes maintenance data for reports.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
